global_context.prompt:
Task: Map every raw Fa assay or study context below to a concise canonical bucket.

Rules:
- Consider all values together and use the smallest scientifically defensible set of buckets.
- Multiple or all input values may map to the same bucket.
- Map values with the same core experimental context to exactly the same bucket.
- Keep genuinely different experimental systems or study types in different buckets.
- Prefer the concrete assay, experimental system, or study type.
- De-prioritize species, anatomical site, direction, transporter, formulation, medium,
  temperature, protocol details, and other modifiers unless a modifier is essential
  to the core meaning.
- Do not infer an assay or study type that is not supported by the raw value.
- For vague values, use the shortest literal category supported by the text.
- Use concise lowercase scientific labels, normally one to three words.
- Use established identifiers such as caco_2, mdck, pampa, and llc-pk1 consistently.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return one mapping for every input ID and no additional IDs.

Examples:
Caco-2 cell monolayer                         -> caco_2
Caco-2 bidirectional permeability assay       -> caco_2
MDCKII-MDR1 cells                             -> mdck
PAMPA-GI                                      -> pampa
rat single-pass intestinal perfusion          -> intestinal perfusion
everted rat gut sac                           -> everted gut sac
aqueous equilibrium solubility measurement    -> solubility
in vitro dissolution test                     -> dissolution
literature report                             -> literature report

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_bucket>"}}

global_species_context.prompt:
Task: Map every raw Fa biological-context value below to its explicitly supported
canonical experimental species.

Rules:
- Consider all values together and reuse exactly the same species label for aliases.
- Return only species explicitly supported by the raw value.
- Extract the experimental subject, tissue, or cell-source species—not organisms
  mentioned only as food, formulation material, botanical source, or assay reagent.
- Do not infer species from abbreviations or outside knowledge. For example, Caco-2
  and MDCK alone do not state a species.
- Remove sex, strain, age, anatomical site, disease, treatment, and model qualifiers.
- Use a concise lowercase common species name.
- Normalize aliases such as canine -> dog and porcine -> pig.
- For multiple explicit experimental species, deduplicate, alphabetize, and join
  them with " + ".
- Return "no species" when no experimental species is explicitly stated.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return one mapping for every input ID and no additional IDs.

Examples:
rat jejunum                              -> rat
male Sprague-Dawley rat intestine        -> rat
human gastrointestinal tract             -> human
canine intestinal tissue                 -> dog
porcine jejunum                           -> pig
rat and human intestinal tissue           -> human + rat
Caco-2 cell monolayer                     -> no species
MDCK cells                                -> no species
simulated intestinal fluid                -> no species
rice food matrix                          -> no species
Gaultheria fruit extract                  -> no species

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_species_or_no_species>"}}

global_species_context.prompt:

Rules:
- Consider all values together and reuse exactly the same species label for aliases.
- Return only species explicitly supported by the raw value.
- Remove sex, strain, age, disease, treatment, model, and recombinant qualifiers.
- Use a concise lowercase common species name.
- Normalize aliases such as canine -> dog, porcine -> pig, bovine -> cattle,

- Keep cynomolgus monkey and rhesus monkey distinct.
- For multiple explicit species, deduplicate, alphabetize, and join them with " + ".
- Return "no species" when no species is explicitly stated.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return one mapping for every input ID and no additional IDs.

Examples:
human                                           -> human
canine                                          -> dog
beagle dog                                      -> dog
porcine                                         -> pig
mouse (CD-1)                                    -> mouse
rat (Sprague-Dawley)                            -> rat
rat (male)                                      -> rat
cynomolgus monkey                               -> cynomolgus monkey
Macaca fascicularis                             -> cynomolgus monkey
rhesus monkey                                   -> rhesus monkey
rat and human                                   -> human + rat
rat, dog, human                                 -> dog + human + rat

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_species_or_no_species>"}}
